chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes junub at the beginning of the night, then sleeps until morning in the month of Ramadan. He said: There is no penalty upon him. I said: But he woke up, then slept again until morning. He said: He must make up that day as a penalty.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no penalty upon him
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes junub (enters state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person wakes up in a state of junub during Ramadan and then goes back to sleep?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar distinguishes between involuntary sleep, which exempts one from penalty, and negligent sleep after waking, which incurs a 'ukubah' (penalty) for missing the fast. Shia jurists interpret this 'ukubah' as a compensatory fast rather than a punitive fine, emphasizing personal responsibility in maintaining ritual purity during Ramadan. The hadith highlights the practical legal nuance between mere occurrence of junub and the failure to perform ghusl promptly upon waking.
